_help: Correction codes, matched to the course correction code (2025). 'codes' are practised in the app. 'otherCodes' are shown in the code key only. 'fullHintEarly': true gives the code AND the rule together at hint 2 (for codes that are not rule-based, like ww and SS). If you rename a code, also change it in the practice texts, data/warmup.json and data/links.json.

codes.name: Wrong tense
codes.meaning: The verb is in the wrong time (past, present or future).
codes.wrong: Last week I go to the library.
codes.right: Last week I went to the library.
codes.rule: Look for time words (last week, since, now). Choose the tense that matches them.

codes.name: Verb form error
codes.meaning: You have used the wrong form of the verb.
codes.rule: Check what comes before the verb: has needs a past participle, is needs -ing, enjoy needs -ing, want needs to + verb.

codes.name: Subject-verb agreement error
codes.meaning: The verb does not match its subject (singular or plural).
codes.wrong: The results of the study shows a clear trend.
codes.right: The results of the study show a clear trend.
codes.rule: Find the main noun of the subject. Singular subject: verb + s. Plural subject: no s.

codes.name: Missing or incorrect article
codes.meaning: A, an or the is missing, wrong or not needed.
codes.right: The Moon moves around the Earth.
codes.rule: Singular countable nouns need a, an or the. Use the when there is only one, or when the reader knows which one.

codes.name: Number (singular / plural)
codes.meaning: Make the noun plural or singular.
codes.wrong: There are many reason for this.
codes.right: There are many reasons for this.
codes.rule: After many, several, a few, numbers above one and a range of, use a plural noun.

codes.name: Uncountable / countable
codes.meaning: The noun is uncountable (no a/an, no plural) or countable, and it is used the wrong way.
codes.rule: Uncountable nouns (information, advice, research, equipment) have no plural and no a or an. Use much, some or a lot of with them.

codes.name: Wrong preposition
codes.meaning: The small linking word (in, on, at, for, to...) is wrong.
codes.rule: Many verbs, nouns and adjectives have a fixed preposition. Learn them as a pair: depend on, interested in.

codes.name: Wrong form
codes.meaning: The word family is right, but the type of word (noun, verb, adjective, adverb) is wrong.
codes.wrong: It is very importance to sleep well.
codes.right: It is very important to sleep well.
codes.rule: Ask what the sentence needs here. After the: a noun. After be or very: an adjective. To describe a verb: an adverb.

codes.name: Wrong word
codes.meaning: The word is a real word, but it is not the right one here. Use another word.
codes.wrong: We need to do a decision soon.
codes.right: We need to make a decision soon.
codes.rule: Some words always go together (make a decision, do research). Check a learner's dictionary for common partners.

codes.name: Incorrect word order
codes.meaning: The words are correct, but they are in the wrong order. Rearrange them.
codes.wrong: I do not know where is the station.
codes.right: I do not know where the station is.
codes.rule: Use subject + verb order in statements and in questions inside sentences. Put always and often before the main verb, but after be.

codes.name: Wrong punctuation
codes.meaning: A comma, full stop, apostrophe or question mark is missing or wrong.
codes.wrong: However the results were its main strength.
codes.right: However, the results were its main strength.
codes.rule: Check commas after linking words, apostrophes for owning (the student's book) and it's (it is), and question marks.

codes.name: Problems with sentence structure
codes.meaning: This sentence does not follow the correct sentence structure. Parts are joined wrongly or mixed up.
codes.wrong: The rent was high, I moved.
codes.right: The rent was high, so I moved.
codes.rule: Join two full sentences with a full stop, a semicolon or a joining word (and, but, so), not just a comma. Use although or but, not both.

codes.name: Incomplete sentence
codes.meaning: This is not a full sentence. It is missing a main clause or a main verb.
codes.wrong: Because the rent was high. I moved.
codes.right: Because the rent was high, I moved.
codes.rule: Every sentence needs a subject and a main verb. A because, which or to clause cannot stand alone: join it to a main clause.

codes.name: Add something
codes.meaning: A word is missing here. Add it.
codes.right: The library is open until 9 pm.
codes.rule: Read the sentence aloud slowly. Check that every clause has a subject and a full verb (is, are, have, be).

codes.name: Omit
codes.meaning: A word here is not needed. Take it out.
codes.rule: Some verbs take an object directly, with no preposition (discuss, enter, contact). Do not repeat a meaning (return back).

otherCodes.name: Reference not clear
otherCodes.meaning: It is not clear what a pronoun (it, this, they) refers to.

otherCodes.name: Link error
otherCodes.meaning: The linking word (however, therefore, in addition) is wrong or missing.

otherCodes.name: Informal
otherCodes.meaning: This is too informal for academic writing.

otherCodes.name: Sentences not in logical order
otherCodes.meaning: The ideas are not in a logical order.

otherCodes.name: Paragraph error
otherCodes.meaning: You need a new paragraph, or you need to revise your paragraph.

otherCodes.name: Meaning unclear
otherCodes.meaning: The meaning of this phrase or sentence is not clear. Consider rewriting it.

otherCodes.name: Irrelevant information
otherCodes.meaning: This information does not belong here.

otherCodes.name: Illegible
otherCodes.meaning: Poor handwriting makes this difficult to read.

otherCodes.name: Join up
otherCodes.meaning: Join these words or parts together.
